trial_court: Court of Ld. Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hoshiarpur and case number: 18.08.2018
case_name: Gaganjit Singh Walia And Ors v. State Of Punjab And Ors

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Gaganjit Singh Walia & others (husband, wife, etc.)

facts_of_case: FIR No.77 dated 06.06.2013 under Sections 498-A IPC and 406 IPC was registered against the petitioners. The parties have arrived at a compromise dated 12.07.2018.

legal_principles.principle: A compromise between parties can be a valid and genuine settlement.
legal_principles.held: The compromise has been executed by the parties out of their free will and without any fear, threat, coercion or undue influence and the same is genuine and valid.

legal_principles.principle: A compromise can be a valid reason to quash proceedings.
legal_principles.held: Thus, no useful purpose would be served to continue with the proceedings in the instant FIR.
cited_cases: Gold Quest International Private Ltd. vs. State of Tamil Nadu and others, (2014)

outcome.final_order: The FIR No.77 dated 06.06.2013 under Sections 498-A IPC and 406 IPC was quashed, and all further proceedings arising therefrom were also quashed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing FIR
advising on compromise agreements in criminal cases
